item.title: Bhikkhus, just as at the end of the summer, when all the grain has been gathered into the barn, a cowherd, tending the cows, sitting…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, just as at the end of the summer, when all the grain has been gathered into the barn, a cowherd, tending the cows, sitting at the root of a tree or in the open, might think about what needs to be done, and thinks: 'These are the cows.' So too, bhikkhus, there was what needed to be done, and I thought: 'These are the states.'
Bhikkhus, I exerted myself, was energetic, not passive, mindfulness was established without confusion, my body was tranquil, without agitation, my mind was concentrated and unified.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 19 – Dvedhāvitakkasutta

item.title: Just as, sisters, there is a great tree standing with heartwood, with roots that are impermanent, subject to change; with a trunk that is impermanent,…
item.description:
Just as, sisters, there is a great tree standing with heartwood, with roots that are impermanent, subject to change; with a trunk that is impermanent, subject to change; with branches and leaves that are impermanent, subject to change; with its shadow that is impermanent, subject to change. If someone were to say: 'This great tree standing with heartwood has roots that are impermanent, subject to change; a trunk that is impermanent, subject to change; branches and leaves that are impermanent, subject to change; but its shadow is permanent, everlasting, eternal, not subject to change' — would that person be speaking correctly?" "No, venerable sir." "Why is that?" "Venerable sir, this great tree has roots that are impermanent, subject to change; a trunk that is impermanent, subject to change; branches and leaves that are impermanent, subject to change; let alone its shadow — that too is impermanent, subject to change!" "That is correct, sisters! If someone were to say: 'These six internal bases are impermanent, and the feeling — pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that arises dependent on these six internal bases is permanent, everlasting, eternal, not subject to change' — would that person be speaking correctly?" "No, venerable sir." "Why is that?" "Venerable sir, dependent on this and that condition, this and that feeling arises. With the cessation of those conditions, those feelings cease and pass away." "Good, good, sisters! That is indeed the true perception of a noble disciple with right wisdom.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 146 – Nandakovādasutta

item.title: - Bhikkhus, form is impermanent, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past form,…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, form is impermanent, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past form, does not delight in future form, and for present form practices for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation. Bhikkhus, feeling is impermanent ... perception is impermanent ... formations are impermanent ... Bhikkhus, consciousness is impermanent, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past consciousness, does not delight in future consciousness, and for present consciousness practices for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.9

item.title: Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple shaves off his hair and beard, puts on the yellow robe, and thinks of going forth from home to homelessness,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple shaves off his hair and beard, puts on the yellow robe, and thinks of going forth from home to homelessness, at that moment, bhikkhus, a divine shout arises among the devas: 'This noble disciple intends to do battle with Māra!' This, bhikkhus, is the first divine shout that arises from time to time among the devas.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, when a noble disciple dwells devoted to developing the seven factors of enlightenment, at that moment, bhikkhus, a divine shout arises among the devas: 'This noble disciple does battle with Māra!' This, bhikkhus, is the second divine shout that arises from time to time among the devas.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, when a noble disciple, by the destruction of the taints, in this very life, with direct knowledge, realizes, attains, and abides in the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, at that moment, bhikkhus, a divine shout arises among the devas: 'This noble disciple has won the battle! Standing at the head of the battle, having been victorious, he dwells.' This, bhikkhus, is the third divine shout that arises from time to time among the devas.

From: Itivuttaka 82

item.title: Who is infatuated with women, with drink, with gambling, And squanders all he has — that is the cause of downfall. Who is not content…
item.description:
Who is infatuated with women, with drink, with gambling,
And squanders all he has — that is the cause of downfall.

Who is not content with his own wife, and is seen with prostitutes or others' wives —
That is the cause of downfall.

Who, having passed youth, takes a young, still-breasted wife
And cannot sleep from jealousy — that is the cause of downfall.

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.6

item.title: At that time, Prince Bodhi, expecting the Blessed One's arrival, was standing at the outer gate. Prince Bodhi saw the Blessed One coming from afar.…
item.description:
At that time, Prince Bodhi, expecting the Blessed One's arrival, was standing at the outer gate. Prince Bodhi saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, he went to meet him, paid homage, and led the way to the Kokanada palace. Then the Blessed One stood at the lowest step. Prince Bodhi said to the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One step on the cloth, let the Well-Gone step on the cloth, so that I may have long-term happiness and welfare." When this was said, the Blessed One remained silent. A second time, Prince Bodhi said... A third time, Prince Bodhi said: "Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One step on the cloth, let the Well-Gone step on the cloth, so that I may have long-term happiness and welfare." Then the Blessed One looked at Venerable Ānanda. Venerable Ānanda said to Prince Bodhi: "Prince, have the cloth rolled up. The Blessed One does not walk on cloth. The Tathāgata has regard for the lower people." Then Prince Bodhi had the cloth rolled up and had seats prepared on the upper floor of the Kokanada palace. Then the Blessed One ascended the Kokanada palace and sat down on the prepared seat with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 85 – Bodhirājakumārasutta

item.title: Delighting in the Dhamma, joyful in the Dhamma, Established in the Dhamma, knowing how to investigate the Dhamma, Not engaging in talk that defiles the…
item.description:
Delighting in the Dhamma, joyful in the Dhamma,
Established in the Dhamma, knowing how to investigate the Dhamma,
Not engaging in talk that defiles the Dhamma,
Led by the well-spoken, truthful words of the teacher.

One who, delighting in the Dhamma taught by the noble ones,
Is unsurpassed in speech, mind, and action,
At peace, gentle, established in jhāna,
Attains the core of wisdom from the heard Dhamma.

From: Sutta Nipāta 2.9

item.title: Bhikkhus, here a bhikkhu, reflecting wisely, does not consent to an arisen sensual thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, and makes it disappear. He does not…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, here a bhikkhu, reflecting wisely, does not consent to an arisen sensual thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, and makes it disappear. He does not consent to an arisen thought of ill-will ... He does not consent to an arisen thought of harmfulness; he abandons, dispels, destroys, and makes it disappear. He does not consent to any arisen evil, unwholesome states; he abandons, dispels, destroys, and makes them disappear.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 2 – Sabbāsavasutta

item.title: I do not see any other single factor, bhikkhus, that leads to such great benefit as a mind that is tamed, guarded, restrained, and protected.…
item.description:
I do not see any other single factor, bhikkhus, that leads to such great benefit as a mind that is tamed, guarded, restrained, and protected. A tamed, guarded, restrained, and protected mind, bhikkhus, leads to great benefit.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.40

item.title: Thus, bhikkhus, disenchantment and dispassion have the knowledge and vision of liberation as their purpose, the knowledge and vision of liberation as their benefit; true…
item.description:
Thus, bhikkhus, disenchantment and dispassion have the knowledge and vision of liberation as their purpose, the knowledge and vision of liberation as their benefit; true knowledge and vision have disenchantment and dispassion as their purpose, disenchantment and dispassion as their benefit; concentration has true knowledge and vision as its purpose, true knowledge and vision as its benefit; happiness has concentration as its purpose, concentration as its benefit; tranquility has happiness as its purpose, happiness as its benefit; rapture has tranquility as its purpose, tranquility as its benefit; joy has rapture as its purpose, rapture as its benefit; non-regret has joy as its purpose, joy as its benefit; good virtues have non-regret as their purpose, non-regret as their benefit. Thus, bhikkhus, (these) conditions lead to (other) conditions; conditions complete (other) conditions, leading from the near shore to the far shore.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.2
